status: Native request-count and concurrency regression fixed and delivered in 0.19.2; production transport and consumer evidence belongs to sdk-0.19.2-delivery.json.

productionTrigger.outcome: Guest cursor timeout, exit 1, scoped sandbox reclaimed.

runtime: Native Alchemy workerd/R2/Queue with real bindings. Request tracing forwards every operation to the same native bucket owner; no mocked R2 or fabricated receipts.

candidate.initialReadAcquisition: Three native get calls begin before their receive events; the root lifetime, process receipt and input body are independent.

focused.scope: Before consolidating head/put assertions into one exact-count assertion; the final full suite validates the current harness.

preserved: Exactly one current-root recheck before conditional publication, in addition to admission lifetime validation.
Capability expiry is checked again before publication.
Native input ETag still serializes append, resize and close.
An exact replay returns its receipt without another write.
Persisted input head and immutable blob contain the accepted bytes.
Read-only capabilities are rejected without bucket requests.
A disposed sandbox rejects the mutation and causes no puts.
Missing-head recovery still requires execute authority and conditional initialization.
The existing bounded size, chunk sum and terminal-control consistency decoder remains the single policy owner.
limits: The successful append drops one R2 request; this is not a production latency or billing comparison.
Metadata reads can already be in flight when a lifetime check rejects a disposed sandbox.
Successful production binding/HTTP cases are recorded separately; they do not erase the historical 0.19.1 failures or prove transport-wide latency guarantees.
existingRecoveryRegression: tests/terminal-resize.test.ts deletes the real input head, rejects readonly initialization, recovers with execute authority and checks resize/close ETag races.

benchmark.scope: Native local workerd warm workloads on a shared host; no production latency or billing comparison.
